articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Meta's AI support bot just got socially engineered into handing over Obama's Instagram to Iranian trolls. When your chatbot has more security clearance than your actual security team, maybe it's time to rethink things.

articles.title: Internet Age-Gates Are a Growing Global Threat
articles.summary: CISA contractor dumped AWS GovCloud keys on public GitHub like it was their personal dev playground. The agency tasked with protecting America's infrastructure just leaked the keys to the castle—chef's kiss level operational security.

articles.title: EFF Testifies to Congress on Protecting Americans’ Rights from Government AI
articles.summary: Trump appoints unqualified DNI while Section 702 warrantless mass spying powers face reauthorization. EFF reminds us why giving surveillance tools to incompetent authoritarians is a historically bad idea.

articles.title: World Food Programme breach exposes data of 600k vulnerable Gazan families
articles.summary: Another Cisco SD-WAN zero-day is being actively exploited with no patch available. Cisco's motto should be 'Pwning the Connected World'—at least they're consistent.

articles.title: AI Agent Uncovers 21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg; Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs
articles.summary: CISA adds actively exploited SolarWinds Serv-U vulnerability to KEV catalog. Because if there's one company that needed more security problems, it's definitely SolarWinds.

articles.title: Miasma Worm Hits 73 Microsoft GitHub Repositories in Major Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary: AI agent autonomously discovers 21 zero-days in FFmpeg while Chrome patches a record 429 bugs. The robots are getting scary good at finding holes—at least they're on our side for now.

articles.title: Zcash faces governance concerns after emergency hard fork over critical vulnerability
articles.summary: Miasma worm hits 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories in massive supply chain attack. Microsoft's own repos got pwned—turns out even Big Tech can't escape the universal law of 'trust but verify.'

articles.title: Two men shot at Trump's Butler rally sue federal government over Secret Service 'preventable failures'
articles.summary: University of Toronto researchers build autonomous AI worm that can reason and adapt to find vulnerabilities. Academic proof-of-concept today, nation-state cyber weapon tomorrow—the future is beautifully terrifying.

articles.title: IITs deny JEE Advanced data breach; CBSE files plaint over cyber attacks
articles.summary: CISA confirms hackers are actively exploiting patched SolarWinds Serv-U flaw to crash servers. SolarWinds: the gift that keeps on giving—like herpes, but for enterprise infrastructure.

articles.title: No data breach: IIT Roorkee rubbishes claims of privacy violation affecting JEE Advanced 2026 students
articles.summary: Five Eyes warns Chinese spies are using fake LinkedIn recruiter profiles to target government and military personnel. Nothing says 'sophisticated nation-state actor' like sliding into someone's DMs with a too-good-to-be-true job offer.
